texts.preamble: The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11 February, 2010 1 In The Court Of Ms. Veena Rani Metropolitan Magistrate Patiala House Courts, New Delhi. In Re :412/1 ( Date of filing :25-09-2009) Megha Modani v. Piyush Modani & others. Complaint under the Protection of women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 P.S.- Hauz Khaas. The Order
texts.facts: 1. The present application u/s. 12 of the Protection of women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 has been filed on 23.09.2009 by Ms. Megha Modani (the applicant-wife) against : Sh. Piyush Modani (husband as R-1); Smt. Jayshree Modani (mother-in-law as R-2); Smt. Ritu Kuchhal (sister-in- law as R-3) ; Sh. Arjun KUchhal ( husband of sister-in-law as R-4). The Protection of women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 would be referred as the Act, 2005. 2. By way of this petition the following orders have been sought by the applicant-wife: a. The protection orders u/s 18 of the Act, 2005; b. The residence orders u/s 19 of the Act, 2005; c. The monetary relief u/s 20 of the Act, 2005; d. The compensation and damages u/s 22 of the Act, 2005; 2 e. The interim order u/s 23 of the Act, 2005; and f. such interim order or orders as deemed fit just and proper in the circumstances of the case. The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11 February, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89556447/ 1 3. The complainant-wife has specifically asked for the following monetary relief(s): a. Rs.20,00000/- (Rupees Twenty Lac) on account of loss of earnings; b. Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) per month towards the medical expenses; c. Rs.10,000/- (Rupees Ten Thousand) per month towards the expenses of food, clothing, medication etc,; d. Rs.20,000/- (Rupees Twenty Thousand) per month towards the household expenses; and e. Rs.30,00,000/- (Rupees Thirty Lac) Thousand) towards the destruction, damage or removal of the any property from the control of the aggrieved person. 4. By way of the present order I shall dispose of the interim order(s) as deemed necessary under S.23(1) of the Act, 2005. 5. The averments made in the application has mentioned that the marrioage of the applicant took place on 01.03.2009. It has been specifically mentioned that though the arrangements in the marriage were impressive & imposing the respondents remained unhappy and utterly dissatisfied. The frequent demands for the dowry started pouring in soon after the marriage. The agony of the applicant was furthered by the beatings and the ill-treatment in the hands of the said respondents. The respondent-husband remained unwilling to have physical relationship with the applicant. The mother-in- law of the applicant often told the respondent No.1 not to sleep with the applicant. 6. As per the averments of the applicant the agonies continued and the husband would very often threaten her with divorce. Many incidences of irrational behavior on part of the respondent-husband have been averred. On one occasion the husband drove very recklessly on the roads almost banging the car against the side lane. On other occasions the husband would behave as a maniac often accompanied by violent outbursts. The applicant is averred to have been subjected to ruthless beatings. The applicant has also averred various incidences of physical violence when the respondents have been brutal to the applicant. The applicant has narrated various incidents where she had subjected to the domestic violence. The complainant has averred to have been subjected from time to time to the: "physical abuse"; "verbal and emotional abuse"; "economic abuse". The complainant had been subjected to insults, ridicule, humiliation and name calling. The complainant has averred deprivation of all economic & financial resources to which the aggrieved person was entitled to. The application has been supported by an affidavit. The Present Application U/S. 12 Of The ... vs Unknown on 11 February, 2010 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/89556447/ 2 7. The applicant has also mentioned that she had approached a counselor in order to seek advice. The respondent-husband is said to have been uncooperative. in the para No.44 of the application / compliant that she has learnt from reliable sources that the respondent-husband suffers from a psychiatric disorder. 8. The respondents have not filed any reply to the application of the applicant. 9. The applicant has raised several contentious issues.
texts.arguments: c. It is, therefore, proposed to enact a law keeping in view the rights guaranteed under Articles 14, 15 and 21 of the Constitution to provide for a remedy under the civil law which is intended to protect the woman from being victims of domestic violence and to prevent the occurrence of domestic violence in the society." 11. Keeping the above-mentioned objects & reasons in mind to provide for more effective protection of the rights of women guaranteed under the Constitution who are victims of violence of any kind occurring within the family and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto, the bill was presented before the Parliament which has become the Act after passing the same by the Parliament. For computing maintenance the following test have been laid down by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Jasbir Kaur Sehgal v. District Judge, Dehradun and Ors., 1997 (7) SCC 7, wherein it has been observed thus : 'No set formula can be laid for fixing the amount of maintenance. It has, in the very nature of things, to depend on the facts and circumstances of each case. Some scope for leverage can, however, be always there. The amount of maintenance fixed for the wife should be such as she can live in reasonable comfort considering her status and the mode of life she was used to when she lived with her husband and also that she does not feel handicapped in the prosecution of her case. At the same time, the amount so fixed cannot be excessive or extortionate." 13. In 2005 CRI. L. J. 3889 "Gurmeet Kour v. Amrik Singh" the Hon'ble J& K HIGH COURT had observed : "At the time of deciding the question of grant of interim maintenance the Court is not entitled to take into consideration the ultimate possibility of dismissal of main application for grant of maintenance. The grounds of defense which are subject to the proof cannot be taken into consideration at that stage by the Court." 14. In Bhagwan v. Kamla Devi (AIR 1975 SC 83) it was observed that the wife should be in a position to maintain standard of living which is neither luxurious nor penurious. 15. The applicant has also mentioned about her jewelry articles kept with the respondents. In a report "The Battered Women's Justice Project, Civil Office" by Christine Thomas (Staff Attorney, BWJP Civil Office, June 2004) it was stated that effective strategies to end violence against women must include strong measures that promote economic security and restitution for survivors. The report by Christine Thomas concluded with the remarks: "Because economic dependence and severe financial stress on abused women can so acutely impact a survivor's choice to stay or leave an abusive relationship and because economic abuse by batterers is often an aspect of the power and control over their lives, stronger legal advocacy for economic safety and restitution is important to the economic empowerment of battered women and the goal of assuring that women may live free of violence and oppression by their intimate partners.
